t: This is Chester Square, a long, elegant residential garden square in Belgravia. The Grosvenor family developed it, as they did nearby Belgrave and Eaton Squares, and named it after Chester, the city closest to their ancestral home. Many notable people have lived or died on this square. Mary Shelley, author of Frankenstein, died here. Mary of Teck, queen consort to George V, lived here. Others include Lieutenant-General Wilbraham Lennox, the first Royal Engineer to win the Victoria Cross, the politician Geoffrey Lloyd, Bishop George Murray and the novelist Catherine Randolph.
